paper.title: Scalable Thompson Sampling using Sparse Gaussian Process Models

settings.name_in_paper: Batch sequential optimization of f in an RKHS with sub-Gaussian noise (kernelized bandit, batch TS)
unmapped: Each round the learner queries a batch of B_batch points and receives all B_batch noisy observations
Frequentist regret for a fixed f with ||f||_{H_k} <= S and k(x,x') <= 1
settings.definition_quote: A sequential learning policy selects a batch of $B$ observation points $\{x_{t,b}\}_{b\in [B]}$ at each time step $t=1,2,\dots,T$ and receives the corresponding real-valued and noisy rewards $\{y_{t,b}=f(x_{t,b})+\epsilon_{t,b}\}$ ... $\epsilon_{t,b}$ are i.i.d. ... $R-$sub-Gaussian ... $||f||_{H_k}\le \Bc$ ... $k(x,x')\le 1$

algorithms.name: S-GP-TS (scalable batch GP Thompson sampling with SVGP and decoupled sampling)

symbols.a_bar: upper multiplicative approximation constant of the std (Assumption 3)
symbols.eps_apx: additive approximation error bound epsilon on the std (Assumption 3)

conditions: Assumption 3: approximate posterior std within multiplicative constants a_lower, a_bar and additive eps of exact std
Assumption 4: |mu_tilde - mu| <= c_t sigma_t with c_t <= c
Assumption 5: discretization D_t with |f(x)-f(x^(t))| <= 1/t^2 and |D_t| <= C(d,B) t^{2d}

source.label: The:RegretBoundsApproximate
source.quote: Consider S-GP-TS with $\alpha_t = 2\u_{t}(1/(t^2))$. Under Assumptions 1,2,3,4 and 5, the regret defined in (1), satisfies R(T,B;f) \le 30\bar{a}\beta_TB\sqrt{\frac{2T\gamma_T}{\log(1+\frac{1}{\tau})}}+(31\beta_T+\alpha_T)\epsilon TB + 15B\Bc+2B

results.notes: Applies to TS with any approximate GP satisfying Assumptions 3-4. Regret is E[sum f(x*)-f(x_tb)] i.e. pseudo-regret. Horizon treated as anytime since tuning depends only on t.

symbols.gamma_TB: maximal information gain after T*B observations

conditions: Assumptions 3, 4, 5 on approximation quality and discretization
results.notes: Order form of Theorem 1; R is the sub-Gaussian parameter (sigma).

symbols.gamma_TB: maximal information gain after T*B observations

conditions: Matern kernel with nu > d/2 or SE kernel, with Mercer decomposition available
inducing points from an eps_0-close k-DPP (inducing point rule) or eigenfunction inducing features
tuning: Matern, inducing points: m_t ~ T^{2d/(2nu-d)}, M ~ T^{(2nu+d)d/(2(2nu-d)nu)}
Matern, inducing features: m_t ~ T^{d/(2nu)}, M ~ T^{(2nu+d)d/(4nu^2)}
delta = 1/T, eps_0 = 1/(T^2 log T) for inducing points

source.label: The:MatSE
source.quote: Under Assumptions 1 and 2, with the algorithmic parameters, kernels and sampling rules specified in Table 1, S-GP-TS offers $R(T,B;f) = O(B\sqrt{\gamma_T\gamma_{TB}T\log(T)})$.

results.notes: Proved for Matern and SE kernels, stated via information gain. Compute: cost O(B(M+m_T)N_T T + B m_T^2 T^2), polynomial in T but N_T exponential in d. Parameters depend on T so horizon known.

cited_results.setting_description: Kernelized bandit, RKHS norm bound, sub-Gaussian noise, sequential (B=1), exact GP Thompson sampling
